blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Managing time well in a British office is partly about habits and partly about signalling. The habits are simple: arrive a little early, keep meetings to their scheduled length, and send a quick note if you are going to be even five minutes late. The signalling matters just as much — you let people see that you respect their time the way you respect your own.

A senior British colleague will quickly notice who has this habit and who does not. They will rarely comment on it directly, because that would be impolite. Instead, they quietly give more responsibility, and better opportunities, to the people who do not waste a minute of the meeting.

In a culture where direct praise is rare, being trusted with someone else's time is one of the highest compliments the British give. It is offered quietly, without ever being announced.

items.q: According to the text, managing time in a British office is partly about habits and partly about…
items.why: "partly about habits and partly about signalling" — os dois lados são hábito e sinalização.

items.q: What should you do if you are going to be five minutes late?
options: Send a quick note in advance
Ask a colleague to cover for you
items.why: "send a quick note if you are going to be even five minutes late."

items.q: Why do senior colleagues rarely comment directly on someone's punctuality?
options: Commenting on it would be impolite
They prefer to comment in writing
It is not measured at work
items.why: "They will rarely comment on it directly, because that would be impolite."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Punctuality quietly influences who gets opportunities.
Respecting time is a form of professional signalling.
Small time habits carry real weight in British offices.
In the UK, appreciation is always stated openly.
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste que o reconhecimento é silencioso — "direct praise is rare" — logo o autor discordaria de que o elogio é sempre aberto.

items.q: The last paragraph suggests that, in British professional culture,…
options: trust is shown through actions more than through words
responsibility is handed out at random
compliments are given loudly and often
items.why: Inferência: ser confiado com o tempo alheio é "one of the highest compliments", oferecido em silêncio — a confiança aparece em atos, não em palavras.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry revisar as primeiras semanas de um novo gestor. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, three weeks in, I wanted to give you a bit of feedback — and honestly, most of it is positive. There's one thing in particular I've noticed, even though nobody has said it out loud yet.

You end your meetings on time. Every single one. When the half hour is up, you wrap up, you confirm the actions, and you let people get on with their day. It sounds small, but here, that habit gets noticed very quickly.

Two of the senior partners mentioned to me — not to you, of course — that your meetings never overrun. They didn't say it as a compliment, exactly. They just said it as a fact. But I've been here long enough to know what that means. When people start describing your meetings as reliable, that is the point at which they begin to hand you the more sensitive work.

So my advice is simple: keep doing it. Don't let it slip when things get busy, because that's exactly when people are watching. Respecting other people's time here isn't announced — it's rewarded, quietly, with trust.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What specific habit has Harry noticed in the new manager?
options: He ends his meetings on time
He arrives early to the office
items.why: "You end your meetings on time. Every single one."

items.q: Who mentioned the manager's meetings, and to whom?
options: The whole team, to the partners
A client, to the senior partners
items.why: "Two of the senior partners mentioned to me — not to you, of course."

items.q: Harry says the partners described the meetings as a fact rather than a compliment. What does he infer from this?
options: The partners had not really noticed
In this culture, a plain observation like that signals genuine approval
The partners were criticising the manager
items.why: Inferência: elogio direto é raro; descrever as reuniões como confiáveis, como fato, é a forma britânica de aprovar.

items.q: Why does Harry warn him not to let the habit slip when things get busy?
options: Because busy periods are exactly when people are watching
Because the partners will leave the company
Because busy periods have no meetings
Because the schedule changes every week
items.why: "Don't let it slip when things get busy, because that's exactly when people are watching."

items.q: What is the reward Harry links to respecting other people's time?
options: More sensitive work and quiet trust
items.why: Inferência: "they begin to hand you the more sensitive work" e "rewarded, quietly, with trust" — a recompensa é confiança e responsabilidade.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Ending meetings on time is a small habit that earns big trust." A habit is…
items.why: Habit = hábito: um padrão de comportamento repetido, não uma decisão isolada.

items.q: "By finishing on time, you signal that you value everyone's day." To signal here means to…
options: communicate something indirectly through your actions
items.why: To signal = sinalizar: transmitir algo, aqui sem dizer com todas as letras — pelo comportamento.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Please keep the review to its ___ so the next team can start on time."
items.why: Scheduled length = duração marcada; manter a reunião dentro do tempo previsto.

items.q: "Nobody wants to feel that a meeting has wasted their time." To waste time means to…
options: spend it with no useful result
items.why: To waste time = desperdiçar tempo: gastá-lo sem resultado útil.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "When people prove reliable, managers give them more ___ and better projects."
items.why: Responsibility = responsabilidade; é o que se confia a quem se mostra confiável.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns quando se fala de tempo e reuniões. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Let's wrap up here so we don't run over." To wrap up means to…
items.why: Wrap up = encerrar, concluir — fechar a reunião.

items.q: "The call started late and began to run over." To run over means to…
items.why: Run over (também 'overrun') = passar do horário previsto.

items.q: "The deadline has been pushed back to Friday." This means it was…
options: brought forward to an earlier date
items.why: Push back (a deadline) = adiar para uma data posterior; na passiva, soa mais diplomático.

items.q: "Can you block out an hour tomorrow for the review?" To block out time means to…
options: reserve it and keep it free
items.why: Block out (time) = reservar/bloquear um período na agenda para uma finalidade.

items.q: "We're going to run behind unless we start now." To run behind means to…
options: be late or delayed against the plan
items.why: Run behind = estar atrasado em relação ao previsto.
